name: Solberg-Maru Structural Maintenance Full Kit
description:
Solberg-Maru Infrastructure is one of the mid-tier corponations responsible for maintaining Meridian's aging transit tunnels, bridge superstructures, and elevated MagRail support columns — work that is unglamorous, physically demanding, and absolutely essential. Their field crew uniform is issued in two colors: charcoal grey for standard maintenance and safety orange for elevated-risk structural work. This kit is the standard grey issue. The coverall is a single-piece construction in heavy synth-canvas with articulated knees and elbows — pre-bent at the joint so the fabric doesn't bind when climbing or crouching — and a full-length front zipper backed by a magnetic snap storm flap. The Solberg-Maru logo, a stylized arch over a horizontal line (representing bridge over waterway), is heat-pressed in reflective silver on the back and left breast. A four-point harness anchor loop is reinforced into the upper back panel, rated to arrest a sixty-kilogram fall load. The collar is high and snug with a separate magnetic closure, designed to pair with a respirator mask that clips to a dedicated ring at the left collar point.

Underneath is an Ironpass Thermal Work Layer in dark charcoal, moisture-wicking and cut to allow full shoulder rotation. The boots are the Penrose Weld Boot, adapted here for climbing use with extra ankle support and a lug sole rated for rebar, grating, and wet concrete. A full-body tool harness in heavy nylon webbing goes over the coverall — carabiner points at both hips and the chest, with a tool-drop tether system for working at height. The hard hat is white Solberg-Maru branded with a pinned-on personal identification number and, almost always, at least one unauthorized sticker from a band, a political cause, or a neighborhood market. Aug-compatible at the spine and both shoulders: the coverall features a rear channel and bilateral shoulder zips that open cleanly for spinal rigs and shoulder-mounted chrome without compromising the structural integrity of the harness anchor. This is a rig for people who keep the city from falling down.
functionality: Rated fall-arrest harness anchor loop, articulated knees and elbows for climbing and crawling, respirator clip-mount at collar, tool-drop tether harness with multi-point carabiner attachment, aug-compatible rear spine channel and bilateral shoulder zips, high snug collar for respirator seal, lug sole for rebar and wet concrete, thermal base layer for tunnel temperature variance, magnetic storm flap for wind exposure at height
what_it_says: Structural maintenance workers occupy a specific niche in Circuit society — they're not glamorous, they're not customer-facing, and most of the city has no idea they exist until something breaks. The harness and the anchor loop say: I work at height, and I do it right. The unauthorized hard hat sticker says: I am still a person inside this corponation rig. Workers who've been on Solberg-Maru crews for years develop a quiet professional pride — they know the city's skeleton better than anyone.
manufacturer: Solberg-Maru Infrastructure (corponation-issued coverall and harness); Ironpass thermal layer; Penrose Weld Boot
price_range: Φ260–Φ380 (issued; personal component replacement Φ80–Φ140 per item)
story_hooks: A structural maintenance worker doing routine inspection of a MagRail support column discovers that three load-bearing anchors have been replaced with substandard components — and the work order in the system shows the job was completed correctly six weeks ago by a crew that doesn't exist.
The unauthorized sticker on a worker's hard hat turns out to be a tracking device — someone has been mapping every Solberg-Maru crew's movement through the tunnel network for months.

A veteran crew member's personal BCI log, recorded during years of tunnel work, contains acoustic and structural data that proves a section of the city's infrastructure is weeks from catastrophic failure — data that Solberg-Maru's official inspections have somehow missed every single time.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian single-piece coverall in charcoal grey with purposeful articulation—high-collared, broad-shouldered, and cinched at the waist by a heavy nylon tool harness. The silhouette is functional and imposing: reinforced at stress points, visibly designed for climbing and confined spaces. Reflective silver Solberg-Maru arch logo on back and left breast catches light. Layered appearance from integrated thermal undershirt visible at collar and cuffs. White hard hat with pinned identification number and worn stickers completes the profile.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso for movement, but articulated at knees and elbows with pre-bent fabric panels that eliminate binding during crouching or climbing. Snug high collar, fitted at wrists and ankles. Four-point harness anchor loop reinforced into upper back creates a structured, slightly elevated shoulder line.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy synth-canvas coverall (durable, fire-resistant blend); Ironpass moisture-wicking thermal layer underneath in dark charcoal; nylon webbing tool harness; Penrose Weld Boot with lug sole. Reflective silver heat-pressed logo and trim.
physical_description.texture: Rough, canvas-like weave with visible thread; pre-creased at joints from manufacturing. Nylon harness webbing adds tactile contrast. Boots have pronounced tread pattern. Thermal layer beneath has subtle ribbed compression texture visible at collar and cuff edges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey as primary with white hard hat. Reflective silver Solberg-Maru logo and reinforced stitch lines. Stickers on helmet vary (unauthorized band logos, neighborhood market marks, political symbols in secondary colors).
physical_description.closures: Full-length front zipper with magnetic snap storm flap; magnetic snap high collar with dedicated respirator clip ring at left collar point; nylon webbing harness with carabiner attachment points; tool-drop tether system integrated into harness.
distinctive_features: Four-point harness anchor loop rated for 60kg fall arrest, reinforced into upper back
Pre-articulated knees and elbows prevent fabric binding
Dedicated respirator mask clip ring at left collar
Rear channel and bilateral shoulder zips for aug compatibility (spinal rigs, shoulder chrome)
Reflective silver Solberg-Maru arch logo (bridge over waterline motif)
Heavy nylon tool harness with bilateral hip carabiner points and chest attachment
White branded hard hat with pinned-on personal ID number
Unauthorized stickers on helmet (band logos, political symbols, neighborhood markers)
Lug sole boots designed for rebar, grating, wet concrete grip
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—mid-tier corporation-issued field uniform for essential infrastructure work. Solid, standard-issue quality; no luxury markers but clearly maintained and regulation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Structural maintenance worker, MagRail infrastructure crew, essential services. Wearing this signals stability within a mid-tier corporation, physical labor, unglamorous but critical work maintaining the city's aging transit and bridge systems. The unauthorized helmet stickers suggest personality and community affiliation beneath the corporate uniformity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and well-used but maintained; visible wear on knees and elbows from climbing and concrete work. Sticker-laden hard hat shows personality customization. Minor weathering, no major tears—these suits are replaced when functionally compromised, not patched. Dust and concrete powder residue typical.
